Turn spell data into a period panel with primo and ultimo status

Source: R/spells_to_panel.R
spells_to_panel.Rd

Spell data has one row per spell: an education, an address, a benefit period, with a start date, an end date and a status. Most analyses need it as a panel instead: one row per unit and year (or quarter, or month), with the status at the start and at the end of the period. spells_to_panel() does that conversion.

Usage

spells_to_panel(
  data,
  id,
  start,
  end,
  status,
  by = c("year", "quarter", "month"),
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  status_is = c("state", "outcome"),
  ongoing = "ongoing",
  primo = c("previous_ultimo", "first_day")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble with one row per spell.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

start, end

Columns with the first and last day of each spell (Date). A missing end means an ongoing spell.

status

Column with the status of each spell.

by

Period length: "year", "quarter" or "month".

from, to

First and last period in the panel, as a year (e.g. 2015) or a Date in the period. When given, every unit gets the same window, which makes a balanced panel. When NULL, each unit runs from the period of its first start to the period of its last end; ongoing spells run to the latest date found in start and end.

status_is

"state" or "outcome", see Details.

ongoing

Status shown while a spell is running when status_is = "outcome", e.g. "i gang".

primo

"previous_ultimo" (default) or "first_day".

Value

A tibble (a data.table if data is one) with the id columns, year, quarter or month for sub-year periods, and primo and ultimo. Rows are sorted by unit and period.

Details

Two meanings of status are supported, because registers use both:

  • status_is = "state" (default): the status holds for the whole spell, e.g. enrolled, on leave. The status at a point is the status of the spell covering it, and NA if no spell does. Spells are closed intervals, as in expectr::expect_no_overlap().

  • status_is = "outcome": the status is what happened when the spell ended, e.g. passed or dropped out, as in education registers. While a spell is running (start <= point < end, or no end) the status is ongoing. From the end date on, the outcome of the most recently ended spell is carried forward until a new spell starts.

Primo follows the convention of age(): by default primo of a period is the last day of the previous period (31 December for years), so primo of one year equals ultimo of the year before. Use primo = "first_day" for 1 January.

If spells overlap, the spell with the latest start decides the status. In state mode, a message counts the points where this happened; find the spells with expectr::expect_no_overlap(). Rows with a missing start, or an end before the start, are dropped with a message.

Why it is fast

Dates are converted to integer days, and spells are sorted once per unit by start. A compiled pass keeps the running maximum of end dates within a unit, so "is a spell running at this point?" and "which spell ended most recently?" are constant-time lookups. Spells are never expanded to days or periods, so the cost is one sort plus a linear pass over spells and output rows.

See also

expectr::expect_no_overlap() to check spells first, expectr::expect_balanced() to check the resulting panel.

Examples

education <- data.frame(
  cpr    = c("a", "a", "b"),
  start  = as.Date(c("2018-08-15", "2021-08-15", "2019-08-15")),
  end    = as.Date(c("2021-06-20", NA,           "2020-03-01")),
  status = c("passed", "in progress", "dropped out")
)

# status describes the outcome at the end of each spell
spells_to_panel(education, cpr, start, end, status,
                from = 2018, to = 2022,
                status_is = "outcome", ongoing = "in progress")
#> # A tibble: 10 × 4
#>    cpr    year primo       ultimo     
#>    <chr> <int> <chr>       <chr>      
#>  1 a      2018 NA          in progress
#>  2 a      2019 in progress in progress
#>  3 a      2020 in progress in progress
#>  4 a      2021 in progress in progress
#>  5 a      2022 in progress in progress
#>  6 b      2018 NA          NA         
#>  7 b      2019 NA          in progress
#>  8 b      2020 in progress dropped out
#>  9 b      2021 dropped out dropped out
#> 10 b      2022 dropped out dropped out

# status holds during the spell
leave <- data.frame(
  cpr    = "a",
  start  = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-09-01")),
  end    = as.Date(c("2020-08-31", "2021-03-31")),
  status = c("enrolled", "on leave")
)
spells_to_panel(leave, cpr, start, end, status, by = "quarter")
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   cpr    year quarter primo    ultimo  
#>   <chr> <int>   <int> <chr>    <chr>   
#> 1 a      2020       1 NA       enrolled
#> 2 a      2020       2 enrolled enrolled
#> 3 a      2020       3 enrolled on leave
#> 4 a      2020       4 on leave on leave
#> 5 a      2021       1 on leave on leave
